headline: 51 years since Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman's assassination on August 15, 1975
summary: The assassination of Bangladesh's founding father on August 15, 1975, marked a pivotal moment in the nation's history, driven by a complex interplay of political, economic, and military factors.
details: On August 15, 1975, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, the then President of Bangladesh, was assassinated in a pre-dawn military action at his Dhaka home. This swift operation led to the deaths of Mujib and most of his family members by sunrise.

The assassination occurred during a period of significant upheaval, following Bangladesh's shift from a parliamentary pluralistic system to a monolithic presidential rule. This era was marked by political authoritarianism, economic hardship, and growing military resentment.

Mujib's creation of the paramilitary Jatiya Rakkhi Bahini, loyal directly to him, sidelined the regular army, causing humiliation and fear among officers. Senior officers accused him of promoting loyalists over merit, further fueling internal military divisions.

The coup was led by a group of majors and captains, reflecting disillusionment among younger officers. Cabinet minister Khondaker Mostaq Ahmad quickly aligned with the mutineers, declaring himself president and granting them immunity through the Indemnity Ordinance, 1975.

Civil-military relations were central to the assassination. Mujib's government's approach to the armed forces and his efforts to maintain tight civilian control, distrusting military political ambitions, created tensions that ultimately led to the coup.

Despite condemning corruption, Mujib's government became associated with widespread graft and nepotism, eroding public trust. This breakdown in governance and credibility was a significant factor contributing to the military's resentment.

The rise of authoritarianism, a gradual process from 1972 to 1975, saw Mujib's government shift to a one-party rule. This was driven by crisis management, distrust of opposition, and a desire to consolidate power in a war-torn country.

The devastating 1974 famine was a turning point, shattering Mujib's image as the 'father of the nation' and alienating him from the masses. His administration's denial of the severe food crisis and attribution to foreign conspiracies further eroded his moral authority.

headline: UN report warns of Al-Qaeda cells in Bangladesh; police unaware of specific information
summary: A UN Security Council report suggests Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) may be forming cells in Bangladesh, though police officials state they lack specific information on the matter.
details: A UN Security Council monitoring report, dated August 10, has expressed concerns that the Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) may be trying to establish cells in Bangladesh. The report noted AQIS's evolution into a regional terrorist entity, operating through decentralised, small, and scattered cells.

Despite the UN's concerns, police high-ups in Bangladesh stated they do not have any specific information on the matter. Additional Inspector General Khondoker Rafiqul Islam and Anti-Terrorism Unit (ATU) chief Md Rezaul Karim both indicated a lack of complete nationwide data or official communication regarding the UN report.

A senior Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit officer, speaking anonymously, alleged that Bangladesh’s counter-terrorism capacity has suffered due to weakened experienced teams and curtailed surveillance on terrorism suspects. This officer linked the UN's findings to the perceived weakening of counter-terrorism efforts.

Following a nationwide alert after a bomb recovery in Motijheel on July 24, police headquarters ordered heightened security. Senior officials instructed police to strengthen patrols, set up checkpoints, search suspicious individuals and vehicles, and intensify intelligence surveillance.

Recent operations led to the recovery of 11 pipe bombs (IEDs) and other explosives, along with an arrest. Based on information from the arrested individual, another IED in a pressure cooker was recovered from Savar. Dhaka Metropolitan Police confirmed that security has been beefed up and heightened measures are continuing.
